source_ref: Luna-Cortes G, Lopez-Bonilla LM, Lopez-Bonilla JM (2019) PLoS ONE 14(6):e0217758, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0217758 (CC BY 4.0); Table 1 'Items of the scales' (Interpersonal connections on virtual social networks [IC] block, 4 bullets), image only, https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0217758.t001; Table 2 'Reliability and convergent validity' (IC1-IC4 loadings, alpha 0.937), https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0217758.t002; S1 File XLSX headers 'IC 1'..'IC 4', doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0217758.s001; processing script data/lunacortes_2019_vsn_scales.py
note: Item wording transcribed from the PLOS article's Table 1 'Items of the scales', which PLOS publishes only as an IMAGE -- read from the .t001 PNG (same cached image batch_089/090 used for the satisfaction and social_value siblings), so the transcription is a fallible image read and worth a human spot-check. Items 1 and 2 are independently corroborated character-for-character by the article's own prose (section on interpersonal connections: 'As a result of my holydays, I established new relationships with other tourists on my social networks'; 'I kept in contact with other tourists I met during my trip using my social networks'). The source's spelling 'holydays' is kept verbatim, not corrected to 'holidays'. The four IC bullets are unnumbered, so bullet order was taken as the IC1..IC4 numbering Table 2 uses; hence mapping_basis=paper_order. CODE DERIVATION: data/lunacortes_2019_vsn_scales.py lowercases 'IC 1'..'IC 4' to ic_1..ic_4 and melts BY NAME (no positional step); confirmed cell-for-cell, all four live items identical to their namesake S1 columns over 444 respondents. MAPPING EVIDENCE (Step 5b, PARTIAL): live 4-item alpha 0.9371 reproduces the published 0.937 (block identity). Table 2 loadings IC1 0.62 / IC2 0.87 / IC3 0.90 / IC4 0.86 single out IC1; in the live data ic_1 is the weakest indicator on both a 1-factor loading (0.843 vs 0.909/0.907/0.893) and corrected item-total r (0.8138 vs 0.8719/0.8602/0.8577). NOT ESTABLISHED: ic_2/ic_3/ic_4, whose published and observed loadings are near-tied (observed ic_2 0.909 vs ic_3 0.907 is even the reverse of published 0.87 vs 0.90, by 0.002 -- not diagnostic given the paper's full-model robust CFA vs this 1-factor fit, but not supportive either). Their assignment rests on bullet order alone. ADMINISTERED LANGUAGE: interviews were in Spanish (section 3.2) with a four-step forward translation from English (section 3.3), but no Spanish wording is published anywhere in the record -- the sole supplement S1 File is the response XLSX with 22 bare code headers and no Spanish text, and the article prints English only. Fallback: English in base fields, language=Spanish, empty _translated columns, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied. Section 3.3 notes the pre-test replaced some Spanish verbs with easier synonyms, so the administered Spanish is not a strict rendering of this English. SCALE ANCHORS: only endpoints labelled ('from 1-totally disagree, to 7-totally agree', section 3.2); resp 2-6 option_text left blank, not padded. No instructions text printed, so instructions blank. STEP 3b: clean -- 4 items on resp 1-7 matches the Table 1 [IC] block and the dictionary Description; not Self-Cong (4) or ISNCC (4) from the same file, which link A rules out by column name. RIGHTS: wording from a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article; the underlying scale (Riper et al. 2013, cited as the IC source) has no row in instrument_rights_register.csv and no quotable fee, permission, NC, ND or no-redistribution clause was located, so silence-is-permission applies. No register row written (rounds may not write ship rows). COVERAGE: 4 items x 7 resp levels shipped (28 rows); n=444 per item, every item uses all seven levels. SIBLINGS: lunacortes_2019_self_congruity untouched (later round).
